content:
amanda_dev: Heads up — seeing short bursts of Xid spikes + nvlink flaps on a handful of nodes in us-west-3 (gpu-usw3-12/13/19) over the last 30m :eyes:

josh_ops: Yep saw that alert too. Prometheus shows XidSpike > 0.5 for those nodes, but kernel logs also show a transient link reset. Not full ECC.

priya_ml: Jobs on those nodes are mostly long-running training (mixed precision). If we drain aggressively we'll push a lot back into the queue and blow our reserved slots for the day. Cost + SLA risk.

kai_infra: My quick read: looks like NVLink retries => transient IO errors. Past incidents we tried full cordon+drain and ended up with 20% capacity drop in the AZ. Proposal: soft-cordon workflow that stagger-drains across AZs and only fully evicts if Xid errors persist or memtest fails.

amanda_dev: +1. Staggering is key. Suggest rules:
- soft-cordon (kubectl annotate node stripe=soft-cordon) immediately on Xid spike > 3 in 10m
- wait 10m; if errors persist or memtest returns non-zero -> escalate to hard cordon + drain
- when draining, pick nodes across AZs (round-robin) to keep per-AZ capacity >= 70%

josh_ops: We also need a Slurm path. Rough scontrol steps:```
# put node in drain state for Slurm
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-usw3-12 State=DRAIN Reason="xid-spike-auto"
# to clear later
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-usw3-12 State=RESUME
```
Make sure the autoscaler doesn't immediately reprovision identical faulty hardware.

priya_ml: Can we gate hard drain on a quick memtest/fingerprint? I can add a small job that runs memtest86-ish (2m) and reports pass/fail via node-exporter label. PromQL:```
avg_over_time(node_gpu_xid_spike_total{job="gpu-exporter"}[10m]) > 3 and on(node) (node_memtest_status == 1)```
But memtest_status semantics: 0=unknown, 1=fail, 2=pass.

kai_infra: Let's tighten the PromQL:```
(node_gpu_xid_spike_rate[10m] > 0.3) and (max_over_time(node_gpu_nvlink_reset_total[15m]) > 0)```
If this fires, infra-bot should soft-cordon the node and create a ticket in #incidents with node + pod list.

infra-bot: [auto] Alert received: xid-nvlink-usw3. Soft-cordoning gpu-usw3-12. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-health

amanda_dev: For the soft-cordon implementation:
- kubectl annotated marker so schedulers respect a new toleration we add to batch/predictable jobs
- P1 ML jobs should have toleration to continue; batch jobs get drained first
- Add a 2m randomized delay window to avoid simultaneous drains when multiple nodes trigger at once

josh_ops: Also need a fallback to put traffic onto Dedicated pool for tenants who opted in. If drain would cause >10% capacity loss for any tenant, do not drain and instead migrate new jobs to dedicated.

priya_ml: I'll prototype the memtest probe and exporter label. Plan: container job that runs on node via DaemonSet with toleration=master only, reports /metrics node_memtest_status{node="gpu-usw3-12"}=1/2.

kai_infra: I'll work on infra-bot to implement:
1) receive Prometheus alert
2) run memtest probe (if not recent)
3) annotate node with soft-cordon and post pod list
4) schedule staggered hard-drain across AZs if memtest fails or nvlink continues for 30m

amanda_dev: For the rollout: can we test in a low-traffic region (eu-central-2) for 48h, then canary to us-west-1, then full us-west-3?

josh_ops: Yes. Also add a cost dashboard to monitor requeue rate + reserved capacity utilization. If requeues > 5% in 1h we abort auto-drain.

priya_ml: Noted. I'll add metrics: job_requeues_total by queue, reserved_slots_utilization_by_tenant.

kai_infra: I'll open a PR with the runbook changes and the infra-bot patch after the prototype. We should also add a k6 load test to ensure stagger windows don't delay critical scheduling badly.

amanda_dev: Thanks — please tag me on the PR. If we agree, I'll create the incident template and escalate policy for >3 nodes in a single AZ.

josh_ops: Agreed. Quick checklist for PR:
- PromQL alert rules + silence windows
- infra-bot workflow (probe -> annotate -> ticket -> stagger drain)
- k8s annotation + scheduler toleration changes
- Slurm scontrol integration and reason tags
- Rollout plan (eu-central-2 canary)

kai_infra: I'll try to get an initial PR by EOD PST.

amanda_dev: Awesome. For visibility: tagging @ops-team and @ml-platform in the PR.

infra-bot: [auto] Ticket created: INC-8342 — xid-nvlink-auto-cordon. Assigned: kai_infra.

josh_ops: One last note — add an opt-out label (gpu-health:auto-drain=disabled) for teams doing experiments.

priya_ml: Good call.

amanda_dev: Ok closing thread. We'll keep an eye on those nodes and revert manual cordons if infra-bot handles it. :white_check_mark:
